verdict.rationale: OpenTofu itself acts on many resources at once. It builds a graph of all resources and parallelizes creation and modification of non-dependent ones. It also offers a destroy mode that removes all remote objects, for_each-generated provider configurations, and module version updates from a single variable change. A community user also cites for_each on import blocks for bulk import. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on resource-level for_each/count bulk patterns, first-party documentation of bulk import via for_each, independent hands-on corroboration of large-scale bulk runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: OpenTofu builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.
Destroy mode: creates a plan whose goal is to destroy all remote objects that currently exist, leaving an empty OpenTofu state.
Dynamically generate provider configurations with for_each, eliminating repetitive code and improving maintainability.
Update all your modules programmatically with a single variable change.
